# DocHub API

> DocHub is where students of the ULB (Université libre de Bruxelles) share
> course documents with each other: notes, summaries, past exams, exercises.
> Everything is in French. AI agents, scripts and apps are welcome to use it on
> behalf of a student.

## Get access

The catalog and the course search are public. Everything else (courses,
documents, uploads) needs a ULB account. Ask your user to create a token at
https://dochub.be/users/tokens/ and send it with every request:

    Authorization: Bearer dh_...

A token can read everything its user can, and upload documents. It cannot
edit, delete, like or report anything.

## Get data as JSON

Add `?format=json` to these pages:

- `/catalog/` and `/catalog/<faculty>/<program>/.../`: the course catalog. You
  get the sub-categories (with their `url`) and the courses of the category.
- `/search/courses/?q=<text>&format=json&page=1`: search courses by name or by
  code (e.g. `INFO-F101`).
- `/catalog/course/<slug>`: a course and its documents. The slug of a course
  is its ULB code in lowercase, e.g. `info-f101` for INFO-F101. Use the `slug`
  the other pages give you: other spellings redirect to it, but only for GET.
- `/documents/<id>`: one document.

A document has a `status`:

- `processing`: we are still converting it. Its `text_url` and `pdf_url` are
  `null` for now: check again in a few minutes.
- `ready`: you can read it. `text_url` and `pdf_url` are `null` if the file
  has no PDF version (e.g. a zip): only `original_url` is there.
- `error`: we could not convert it, and this will not change. Stop checking.

Errors come as JSON too, as `{"error": "..."}`, when you add `?format=json`.

## Read documents

- `/documents/<id>/text`: the text of the document, page by page, as plain
  text. It is small and fast to read.
- `/documents/<id>/pdf`: the document as PDF.
- `/documents/<id>/original`: the file as it was uploaded.

The text comes from the PDF as it is, with no OCR. Start with it for documents
that are mostly text, but read the PDF when:

- pages are marked `no text, probably a scan or an image`: scans, photos of
  handwritten notes or pictures,
- the document is slides, or has diagrams, charts or tables,
- the document has math formulas: they often come out garbled in the text,
- the text looks mixed up, for example with columns in the wrong order.

Every request to the text, the PDF or the original counts as one document read
in the daily limits below, so pick the right one first.

## Upload a document

Send a `multipart/form-data` POST to
`/documents/upload/<course slug>?format=json` (the exact slug, e.g.
`info-f101`: we do not redirect a POST) with:

- `file`: the file (required)
- `name`: a title (optional, we use the file name otherwise)
- `description`: a few words about it (optional)

You get the new document back as JSON (HTTP 201), or the errors (HTTP 422).
The new document is `processing`: check `/documents/<id>?format=json` until it
is `ready` or `error`.
A file that is already on DocHub is refused.

## Limits

They are the same for a student in a browser and for their tokens, and they
are shared:

- {{ RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE }} requests per minute,
- {{ DAILY_CAPS.downloads }} documents read or downloaded per day (text, PDF or original),
- {{ DAILY_CAPS.uploads }} documents uploaded per day.

Over a limit, you get HTTP 429. Please wait instead of retrying in a loop.
The user can see their usage at https://dochub.be/users/tokens/.

`/users/tokens/?format=json` gives the same usage as JSON: what is `used` of
each daily `limit`, when they reset (`usage_resets_at`), and the tokens of the
user. `current_token` is the token that sent the request.
